records.query: Need the patient's detailed neurological examination findings and brain MRI/EEG results, as these are core for confirming a central neurological disorder and distinguishing it from peripheral vestibular or cardiovascular causes.
records.text: - MRI Findings:       - T1-weighted Images:         Image Description: T1 hyperintensity within the medial component, confirming fat presence. Lateral component at porus acusticus was isointense, without flow voids.       - T2-weighted Images:         Image Description: Complex signal with inhomogeneous signal in both fat and soft-tissue components.       - Postcontrast fat-saturated T1-weighted Images:         Image Description: Nodular enhancement of soft-tissue component and fat saturation of medial component.

records.query: Need the detailed neurological examination findings and EEG results, as the MRI shows a fat-containing lesion at the porus acusticus with soft-tissue enhancement, which may indicate a peripheral vestibulocochlear lesion rather than a central disorder; these additional results are critical to confirm or exclude the leading central neurological hypothesis.

Need the patient's brain MRI report (core imaging to evaluate for central structural lesions such as cerebellar atrophy, white matter disease, or demyelinating plaques) to further confirm central neurological disorder.

Need the patient's neurological examination records and laboratory results (e.g., vitamin B12, thyroid function, autoimmune panel) to exclude metabolic or peripheral mimics, complementing the brain MRI in confirming a central neurological disorder.

Need the patient's audiometry and vestibular function testing results, including pure-tone audiogram, caloric testing, and videonystagmography, to directly evaluate peripheral vestibulocochlear function and corroborate the MRI finding at the porus acusticus; these are essential for confirming a peripheral vestibular disorder.

Need the patient's electroencephalogram (EEG) report to evaluate for central paroxysmal activity, as the shaking episodes could reflect seizure activity, and to help definitively exclude a central neurological cause, complementing the peripheral vestibular evidence already obtained.

Need fat-suppressed MRI and high-resolution heavily T2-weighted cisternography (CISS/FIESTA) of the internal auditory canal to confirm the lesion is fat and to delineate its exact relation to the vestibulocochlear nerve at the porus acusticus; this is critical for validating the suspected lipoma and differentiating it from schwannoma or meningioma, thereby strengthening the peripheral vestibulocochlear disorder and limiting residual central uncertainty.
records.text: Postcontrast fat-saturated T1-weighted Images:         Image Description: Nodular enhancement of soft-tissue component and fat saturation of medial component.

records.query: Need the patient's audiometry and vestibular function test results (pure-tone audiogram, caloric testing, videonystagmography) along with the EEG report, as these are the critical missing studies to directly verify peripheral vestibulocochlear dysfunction and rule out central paroxysmal activity, thereby consolidating the lipoma-induced peripheral disorder and limiting residual diagnostic uncertainty.

bindings.label: A woman in her 50s presented to the emergency department after a fall
Patient reported lifelong clumsiness, worsening difficulty with balance over the past few years, and occasional falls sometimes preceded by vertigo and 'shaking' episodes
MRI shows a fat-containing lesion at the porus acusticus with soft-tissue enhancement
The patient's symptoms are caused by a vestibulocochlear nerve lesion at the porus acusticus
No syncope, palpitations, or loss of consciousness reported
The porus acusticus is the entry point of the vestibulocochlear nerve
Audiometry, vestibular function tests, and EEG results are not available
Peripheral vestibulocochlear disorder due to fat-containing lesion (likely lipoma) at the porus acusticus
Peripheral vestibulocochlear disorder due to vestibular schwannoma at the porus acusticus
Peripheral vestibulocochlear disorder due to meningioma at the porus acusticus
Postcontrast fat-saturated T1 MRI shows soft-tissue enhancement within the fat-containing lesion at the porus acusticus
